topics.name: Homophones used as the right part of speech
Joining sentences (and, because, so, while, who, whose)

options: Papa Panov new that someone would come.
Papa Panov knowed that someone would come.
Papa Panov knew that someone would come.
questions.rule: knew is the past tense of the verb know. new is an adjective (not old).

options: They were the best shoes he had ever made.
They were the goodest shoes he had ever made.
They were the better shoes he had ever made.
questions.rule: good - better - best. 'Ever made' compares with all of them, so use the superlative best.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: grew
growing
grown

questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had grown up.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: that
than
as

questions.rule: A comparative is followed by than: more miserable than ever. 'Then' is about time.

options: here
hear
heard
questions.rule: We need a verb after Did you: hear. 'Here' tells a place.

options: bigger
biggest
more big
questions.rule: Comparing two things with than needs the comparative: bigger.
so joins a reason to its result: He was tired, so he slept.

chat: Did you see the Christmas play?
options: No, it had ended before I reached the hall.
No, it had end before I reached the hall.
No, it has ended before I reached the hall.
questions.rule: The play ended first, so use the past perfect: had ended.

questions.source: No other shoes were as good as these.
options: These shoes were gooder than any other shoes.
These shoes were best than any other shoes.
These shoes were better than any other shoes.
questions.rule: The comparative of good is better, followed by than any other.

questions.source: Papa Panov made coffee. He gave it to the sweeper.
options: Papa Panov made coffee and give it to the sweeper.
Papa Panov made coffee and gave it to the sweeper.
Papa Panov made coffee and gave them to the sweeper.
questions.rule: Both verbs stay in the past (made ... gave), and coffee is it.

options: I no the way to the next village.
I knows the way to the next village.
I know the way to the next village.
questions.rule: know is the verb; no is a negative word. With I, use know (no -s).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The bells had start ringing before Papa Panov woke up.
The bells had started ringing before Papa Panov woke up.
The bells has started ringing before Papa Panov woke up.
questions.rule: The bells began first, so had started; the later action stays in the simple past.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: whose
whom
which

questions.rule: The sweeper's clothes = whose clothes. Use whose to show belonging.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: kindness
kinds
kindest

questions.rule: the ... in the whole village compares with everyone, so use the superlative kindest.

options: because of
so
despite
questions.rule: Having no money is the reason; not buying shoes is the result. A result clause is joined with so.

options: through
threw
thorough
questions.rule: We need a preposition: through. 'Threw' is the past of throw.
Past perfect = had + past participle: had walked.

chat: Is Pune colder than Mumbai in December?
options: Yes, Pune is much more colder than Mumbai.
Yes, Pune is much colder than Mumbai.
Yes, Pune is much coldest than Mumbai.
questions.rule: Short adjectives add -er: colder. Never use 'more' with an -er word.

options: Yes, I am hear. Please come in.
Yes, I am here. Please come in.
Yes, I is here. Please come in.
questions.rule: here tells the place; hear is a verb (listen). With I, use am.

questions.source: The girl was walking to the next village. She needed work.
options: The girl was walking to the next village because she need work.
The girl was walking to the next village because her needed work.
The girl was walking to the next village because she needed work.
questions.rule: because joins the reason; keep the subject pronoun she and the past tense needed.

options: The further he read, the sleepier he became.
The further he read, the sleepiest he became.
The further he read, more sleepy he became.
questions.rule: In the ... the ... sentences both parts use the comparative: the further ... the sleepier.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: When the girl arrived, Papa Panov had already gave coffee to the sweeper.
When the girl arrived, Papa Panov had already given coffee to the sweeper.
When the girl arrived, Papa Panov has already given coffee to the sweeper.
questions.rule: The earlier action takes had + past participle: had already given.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: looking
looks
looked

questions.rule: had is followed by the past participle: had looked.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: rested
rests
resting

questions.rule: Both actions happened at the same past time, so both are in the past: fed ... while ... rested.

options: hole
wholly
whole
questions.rule: We need an adjective before day: whole (all of it). 'Hole' is a noun.
The superlative happiest comes before the noun; ever closes the sentence.
because introduces the reason: because it was cold.

chat: Why didn't you buy the cake?
options: The shop had closed by the time I got there.
The shop had close by the time I got there.
The shop has closed by the time I got there.
questions.rule: By the time + past points to an earlier action: had closed.

chat: Why are you wearing a sweater?
options: I am wearing it because it is cold today.
I am wearing it because it cold today.
I am wearing it because it are cold today.
questions.rule: The reason after because needs a full clause: it is cold.

questions.source: Papa Panov gave the baby a pair of shoes. Then the girl left.
options: Before the girl left, Papa Panov had given her baby a pair of shoes.
Before the girl left, Papa Panov has given her baby a pair of shoes.
Before the girl left, Papa Panov had gave her baby a pair of shoes.
questions.rule: The earlier action takes had given; the later one stays in the simple past left.

options: Riya through the old box away and bought a new one.
Riya threw the old box away and bought a new one.
Riya threw the old box away and bought a knew one.
questions.rule: threw = past of throw (a verb); new = adjective. 'Through' and 'knew' don't fit.

options: It was one of the coldest days of the winter.
It was one of the coldest day of the winter.
It was one of the colder days of the winter.
questions.rule: one of the + superlative + plural noun: one of the coldest days.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: keeping
kept
keeps

questions.rule: Past perfect passive = had been + past participle: had been kept.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: much
many
most

questions.rule: We strengthen a comparative with much (or far), never with 'very': much more grateful.

options: who
whose
which
questions.rule: The mother's baby = whose baby. Use whose to show belonging.

questions.after: many visitors, but not the one he expected.
options: has met
meets
had met
questions.rule: By evening (a past time) takes the past perfect: had met.
Long adjectives form the comparative with more: more precious than.

chat: Do you know the new boy in your class?
options: Yes, I no him. He is very friendly.
Yes, I know him. He is very friendly.
Yes, I knows him. He is very friendly.
questions.rule: The verb is know (no -s with I). 'No' is not a verb.

chat: Who is the fastest runner in your team?
options: Meera is the faster of us all.
Meera is the most fastest of us all.
Meera is the fastest of us all.
questions.rule: Comparing with the whole group needs the superlative fastest, never 'most fastest'.

questions.source: Papa Panov was the kindest man in the village.
options: No other man in the village was so kinder as Papa Panov.
No other man in the village were as kind as Papa Panov.
No other man in the village was as kind as Papa Panov.
questions.rule: Superlative -> positive: No other ... was as kind as ... (positive form kind).

options: Although he was disappointed, but Papa Panov kept watching the street.
Although he disappointed, Papa Panov kept watching the street.
Although he was disappointed, Papa Panov kept watching the street.
questions.rule: Although already joins the two parts, so don't add 'but'. 'He was disappointed' needs was.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Papa Panov realised that he had seen his visitor many times that day.
Papa Panov realised that he has seen his visitor many times that day.
Papa Panov realised that he had saw his visitor many times that day.
questions.rule: The seeing came before the realising: had seen (had + past participle).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: whose
who
whom

questions.rule: The mother is a person and the subject of had walked, so use who.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: rushed
rushing
rushes

questions.rule: No sooner had ... than + simple past: than the cold air rushed in.

questions.before: Of all the people he helped, the baby was the
options: youngest
younger
more young
questions.rule: Of all compares with more than two, so use the superlative youngest.
that he had kept describes the shoes and comes right after them.

chat: Did you enjoy the story session at the library yesterday?
options: Yes! Until yesterday, I have never heard such a lovely story.
Yes! Until yesterday, I had never hear such a lovely story.
Yes! Until yesterday, I had never heard such a lovely story.
questions.rule: Until yesterday points to a time before a past moment, so use the past perfect: had never heard.

questions.source: Papa Panov was a shoemaker. He lived alone in a little village.
options: Papa Panov, who he lived alone in a little village, was a shoemaker.
Papa Panov, who lived alone in a little village, was a shoemaker.
Papa Panov, which lived alone in a little village, was a shoemaker.
questions.rule: who replaces he, so don't keep both; use who, not which, for a person.

questions.source: Very few villagers were as kind as Papa Panov.
options: Papa Panov was one of the kindest villager.
Papa Panov was one of the kindest villagers.
Papa Panov was one of the kinder villagers.
questions.rule: Very few ... as kind as -> one of the kindest + plural noun.

questions.prompt: Join the sentences using 'As soon as'.
questions.source: Papa Panov saw the beggars. He hurried indoors to fetch soup.
options: As soon as Papa Panov saw the beggars, he hurry indoors to fetch soup.
As soon as Papa Panov saw the beggars, he hurried indoors to fetch soup.
As soon as Papa Panov saw the beggars, so he hurried indoors to fetch soup.
questions.rule: As soon as joins the two actions; no 'so' is added, and both verbs stay in the past.
